acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Insectoids family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Worker, T1, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Resin-Route Initiate (Initiate) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two wind construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Dull matte brown chitin, thin spindly limbs, small mandibles, no weapons, no wings, and a hunched carrying posture.
Signature mechanic: Work Trail: the Worker presses a resin pellet onto one floor node, creating a short visible route another Insectoid may follow faster.
battlefieldDuty: Probe route awareness by carrying one resin pellet between comb markers while avoiding direct confrontation.
constructionDimensions: Tier-safe anatomy: T1–T2 retain no wings with pressure flutes limited to spiracles and limb vanes; T3 retains closed wing cases as sealed pressure chambers; T4 retains functional wings with slotted membrane veins; T5 remains wingless with bellows segments in the abdomen and comb throne.
Force becomes directional through hollow chitin tubes, resin vanes, aligned antennae, counted spiracle pulses, and a still center at the active joint, case seam, wing root, or throne bellows.
counterplay: Strike the exposed middle joint or destroy the pellet before placement; the wingless Worker hunches and retreats without a route. Affinity signal: Antennae and resin vanes align while one spiracle row goes silent; cross the lee or strike that still center before pressure releases.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only pale chitin without flutes, vanes, and directional pressure
Glow-only wind treatment without a force route and still center
Invented wings on T1–T2 or T5 and prematurely open T3 wing cases
Treating ordinary T4 wing membranes or flight alone as Wind affinity
identityInvariants: Segmented chitinous body, mandibled head, compound eyes, four to six limbs, narrow waist, and rear abdomen remain legible across all forms.
Chitin brown and black mature into glossy crimson, iridescent green-black, and amber accents without replacing caste-specific limb shapes.
Chitin, resin, wax comb, translucent wing membrane where anatomically present, and amber remain distinct family materials.
Shell ridging, fluting, resin plating, spiracle vents, and comb-throne structures communicate specialization rather than generic size.
Wing state is tier-specific: T1–T2 have no wings, T3 has closed wing cases, T4 has functional wings, and the immense T5 Queen is wingless.
telegraph: Its dull matte abdomen lowers, thin middle limbs cradle the pellet, and small mandibles point toward the chosen comb marker.
